about: Topic map of the AP Environmental Science Course and Exam Description (effective fall 2026, V.1; content unchanged from the 2019-20 framework apart from wording clarifications), written in LevlPrep's own words from docs/apenv-research/framework.md. Every topic title is official (Course at a Glance poster). Objectives, knowledge lines and the skills each topic is tagged with are our own summaries and tagging, not CED text; the CED extract stops in Topic 3.7, so Units 4-9 detail pages were not read (docs/apenv-needs-author.md, ced-text).

ced.title: AP Environmental Science Course and Exam Description
ced.edition: Effective Fall 2026, V.1 (9 units, 99 topics; minor clarifications only)
ced.verification: All 99 titles from the Course at a Glance poster (agrees with every title the CED extract showed: Units 1-4 in full and most of 5-9). CED text readable to about 112k characters (into Topic 3.7). Practice weights are third party (Wikipedia, Fiveable). Read 2026-10-20.

bigIdeas.name: Interactions Between Different Species and the Environment

skillNames.1.C: Explain environmental concepts and processes in an applied context

skillNames.2.A: Describe the features of a model, diagram or other visual
skillNames.2.B: Explain relationships shown in a model or diagram
skillNames.2.C: Explain how a model or diagram connects to a wider environmental issue

skillNames.3.B: Describe the author's perspective and assumptions
skillNames.3.C: Describe how the evidence supports or refutes the claim
skillNames.3.D: Evaluate the credibility of a source (not assessed)
skillNames.3.E: Evaluate the validity of conclusions (not assessed)

skillNames.4.A: Identify a testable hypothesis or scientific question
skillNames.4.B: Identify a research method, design or measure
skillNames.4.C: Describe an aspect of a research method, design or measure
skillNames.4.D: Make observations or collect data (not assessed)
skillNames.4.E: Explain the effect of a change to a research design

skillNames.5.A: Describe patterns or trends in data
skillNames.5.B: Describe relationships among variables in data
skillNames.5.C: Explain patterns and trends in data to draw conclusions
skillNames.5.E: Explain what data imply for an environmental issue

skillNames.6.A: Choose an approach or method to solve a problem
skillNames.6.B: Apply the method, showing the steps
skillNames.6.C: Calculate an accurate answer, with units

skillNames.7.B: Describe possible responses to an environmental problem
skillNames.7.C: Describe advantages, disadvantages and unintended consequences of a response
skillNames.7.D: Use data and evidence to support a response
skillNames.7.E: Propose and justify a solution to an environmental problem
skillNames.7.F: Justify a solution by explaining how its benefits work

topics.title: Introduction to Ecosystems
objectives: Describe how organisms in an ecosystem interact with each other and with nonliving parts of the environment.
knowledge: An ecosystem is the living community of an area plus its physical environment.
Predation, competition and symbiosis shape which species live where; resource partitioning lets competitors coexist.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Terrestrial Biomes
objectives: Describe how the climate of a region sets its biome and the organisms adapted to it.
knowledge: Average temperature and precipitation determine the major land biomes.
Biomes shift as climate changes; a climatograph summarizes a biome's climate.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Aquatic Biomes
objectives: Describe the major aquatic biomes and the abiotic factors that set what lives in each.
knowledge: Salinity, depth, flow, temperature and dissolved oxygen separate aquatic biomes.
Wetlands, estuaries and coral reefs are among the most productive ecosystems.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: The Carbon Cycle
objectives: Explain how carbon moves among the atmosphere, living things, oceans, sediments and fossil fuels, and how people change those flows.
knowledge: Carbon moves between reservoirs (sinks and sources) through photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, sedimentation and combustion.
The largest reservoirs are sedimentary rock and the ocean; burning fossil fuels moves carbon to the atmosphere faster than it is removed.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: The Nitrogen Cycle
objectives: Explain the steps of the nitrogen cycle, the soil microbes that drive them, and how fixation limits productivity.
knowledge: The atmosphere is the largest nitrogen reservoir, but most organisms cannot use nitrogen gas.
Fixation, nitrification, assimilation, ammonification and denitrification move nitrogen between forms; slow fixation makes nitrogen a limiting nutrient.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries
topics.clarified2026: EK wording refined (2026-27): steps, soil microbes, fixation rate limits productivity, atmosphere the largest reservoir

topics.title: The Phosphorus Cycle
objectives: Explain why phosphorus cycles slowly, through rock and sediment with no important gas phase, and why it limits growth.
knowledge: Rock and sediments are the main phosphorus reservoirs; weathering releases it slowly.
With no significant atmospheric phase, phosphorus is often the limiting nutrient in water.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries
topics.clarified2026: EK wording refined (2026-27): rock and sediment reservoirs, no significant atmospheric phase, slow weathering makes it limiting

topics.title: The Hydrologic (Water) Cycle
objectives: Explain how water moves through evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, runoff and infiltration, and where it is stored.
knowledge: The ocean is the largest water reservoir; most fresh water is ice or groundwater.
Solar energy drives evaporation and transpiration; gravity drives runoff and infiltration.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Primary Productivity
objectives: Calculate and explain primary productivity: gross production, the share used in respiration, and what is left as net production.
knowledge: Gross primary productivity is the total rate of photosynthesis; net primary productivity is what remains after the producers' own respiration (NPP = GPP minus respiration).
Productivity is a rate per area per time and differs widely between ecosystems.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Trophic Levels
objectives: Describe trophic levels and how energy moves from producers to consumers.
knowledge: Each step in feeding is a trophic level: producers, then primary, secondary and tertiary consumers.
Consumers are herbivores, carnivores or omnivores by what they eat.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Energy Flow and the 10% Rule
objectives: Apply the 10% rule to calculate the energy available at each trophic level and explain why most energy is lost as heat.
knowledge: Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level is passed to the next; the rest is used or lost as heat.
Energy, biomass and number pyramids show the losses; the laws of thermodynamics explain them.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Food Chains and Food Webs
objectives: Describe food chains and food webs, including detritivores and decomposers, and predict how removing a species ripples through a web.
knowledge: A food chain is one feeding path; a food web is all the connected paths in an ecosystem.
Detritivores and decomposers return nutrients from dead matter to the soil and water.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries
topics.clarified2026: EK wording refined (2026-27): food chain and web definitions, detritivores and decomposers

topics.title: Introduction to Biodiversity
objectives: Describe the levels of biodiversity and explain why more diverse populations and ecosystems recover better from disturbance.
knowledge: Biodiversity includes genetic, species and habitat diversity; species diversity has richness and evenness.
A population bottleneck cuts genetic diversity; keystone species hold a community together.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Ecosystem Services
objectives: Describe the services ecosystems give people and the economic and ecological cost when people disrupt them.
knowledge: Services are provisioning, regulating, cultural and supporting.
Disrupting an ecosystem has costs that markets often leave out.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Island Biogeography
objectives: Explain how island size and distance from the mainland set species richness, and apply the idea to habitat islands.
knowledge: Larger islands and islands closer to the mainland hold more species.
Habitat fragments act as islands, with the same effects.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Ecological Tolerance
objectives: Describe the range of conditions an organism or population can tolerate and what happens outside it.
knowledge: Each species has an optimal range, zones of physiological stress and zones of intolerance for each factor.
Tolerance applies to individuals and to whole populations.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Natural Disruptions to Ecosystems
objectives: Explain how periodic, episodic and random natural disruptions affect ecosystems, and how sea level and climate have changed over geological time.
knowledge: Natural disruptions can be periodic, episodic or random, and can change ecosystems for a short or long time.
Earth's climate and sea level have changed many times; some organisms migrate in response.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Adaptations
objectives: Explain how populations respond to environmental change through natural selection on heritable traits over generations.
knowledge: Natural selection favors individuals with heritable traits that suit the environment, so the population changes over generations.
Fast environmental change can outpace a population's ability to adapt.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries
topics.clarified2026: Learning objective reworded (2026-27): how populations respond to environmental change through natural selection over generations

topics.title: Ecological Succession
objectives: Describe primary and secondary succession and the role of pioneer species.
knowledge: Primary succession starts on bare rock with no soil; secondary succession starts where soil remains after a disturbance.
Pioneer species arrive first; a mature community is more stable and diverse.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Generalist and Specialist Species
objectives: Compare generalist and specialist species and how each fares when the environment changes.
knowledge: Specialists have narrow niches and are more vulnerable to change; generalists have broad niches.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: K-Selected r-Selected Species
objectives: Compare r-selected and K-selected species by their reproductive traits and how they respond to disturbance.
knowledge: r-selected species have many offspring with little care; K-selected species have few offspring with much care.
r and K strategies are about reproduction; survivorship curves are a separate idea.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Survivorship Curves
objectives: Describe and read the three types of survivorship curves.
knowledge: Type I: most survive to old age; Type II: a constant death rate; Type III: most die young.
A survivorship curve plots survivors on a log scale against age.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Carrying Capacity
objectives: Explain carrying capacity, overshoot and dieback.
knowledge: Carrying capacity (K) is the largest population an environment can support over time.
A population that overshoots K degrades its resources and dies back.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Population Growth and Resource Availability
objectives: Compare exponential and logistic growth and explain how density-dependent and density-independent factors limit populations.
knowledge: With unlimited resources a population grows exponentially (a J-curve); limits bend growth into a logistic S-curve that levels off at K.
Density-dependent factors grow stronger as a population grows; density-independent ones do not.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Age Structure Diagrams
objectives: Read age structure diagrams and predict whether a population will grow, stay stable or shrink.
knowledge: A wide base means rapid growth; a column shape means stability; a narrow base means decline.
A large young cohort keeps a population growing for a time even after fertility falls.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Total Fertility Rate
objectives: Explain total fertility rate, replacement level, and the factors that raise or lower fertility.
knowledge: Total fertility rate is the average number of children a woman has in her lifetime.
Replacement level is about 2.1; education and opportunities for women lower fertility, as does lower infant mortality.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Human Population Dynamics
objectives: Calculate the rate of natural increase from birth and death rates and the doubling time by the rule of 70, and explain limits to human population growth.
knowledge: The rate of natural increase in percent is (crude birth rate minus crude death rate) divided by 10, since both are per 1,000 people.
Doubling time is about 70 divided by the growth rate in percent; Malthus argued population outruns food.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries
topics.clarified2026: EK wording refined (2026-27): rate of natural increase as CBR minus CDR in percent; rule of 70

topics.title: Demographic Transition
objectives: Describe the stages of the demographic transition and the age structure typical of each.
knowledge: Countries move from high birth and death rates (preindustrial) through falling death rates (transitional) and falling birth rates (industrial) to low rates (postindustrial).
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Plate Tectonics
objectives: Describe the three kinds of plate boundaries and the landforms, earthquakes and volcanoes they produce.
knowledge: Convection in the mantle moves tectonic plates.
Convergent boundaries form mountains, trenches and volcanoes; divergent boundaries form rifts and new crust; transform boundaries cause earthquakes.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Soil Formation and Erosion
objectives: Describe how soil forms from parent material, its horizons, and how it is eroded.
knowledge: Weathering of parent material and the decay of organic matter form soil slowly, in horizons.
Wind and water erode soil, faster where vegetation is removed.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Soil Composition and Properties
objectives: Read the soil texture triangle and explain how texture sets porosity, permeability and water-holding capacity.
knowledge: Soil texture is the share of sand, silt and clay; loam has a balance of the three.
Larger particles mean more permeability and less water-holding capacity.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries
topics.clarified2026: EK wording refined (2026-27): soil texture triangle and loam

topics.title: Earth's Atmosphere
objectives: Describe the layers and composition of the atmosphere.
knowledge: The atmosphere is mostly nitrogen and oxygen; the troposphere holds the weather and the stratosphere holds the ozone layer.
Temperature changes direction with height from layer to layer.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Global Wind Patterns
objectives: Explain how uneven heating and Earth's rotation set global wind patterns.
knowledge: Warm air rises at the equator and sinks near 30 degrees, forming Hadley cells; Ferrel and polar cells lie poleward.
The Coriolis effect deflects winds, producing the trade winds and westerlies.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Watersheds
objectives: Describe a watershed and the factors that shape it.
knowledge: A watershed is all the land that drains into one body of water; its area, slope, soil and vegetation shape runoff and erosion.
A watershed is surface land; an aquifer is underground water.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Solar Radiation and Earth's Seasons
objectives: Explain how latitude and the tilt of Earth's axis set insolation and the seasons.
knowledge: Insolation is greatest where sunlight hits most directly, near the equator.
Seasons come from the tilt of Earth's axis, not its distance from the Sun; albedo is the share of sunlight a surface reflects.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Earth's Geography and Climate
objectives: Explain how mountains, oceans and ocean currents shape regional climates.
knowledge: Air forced up a mountain cools and drops its rain on the windward side, leaving a rain shadow behind.
Ocean currents carry heat; land near large water bodies has milder climates.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: El Niño and La Niña
objectives: Compare El Niño and La Niña: trade winds, upwelling, rainfall and the effects on ecosystems.
knowledge: In El Niño the trade winds weaken, warm water spreads east and upwelling off South America drops.
In La Niña the trade winds strengthen, upwelling increases and the eastern Pacific cools.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: The Tragedy of the Commons
objectives: Explain the tragedy of the commons and ways to manage shared resources.
knowledge: When a resource is open to all, each user gains from taking more while the cost is shared, so the resource is overused.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Clearcutting
objectives: Describe clearcutting and its effects on soil, water and wildlife.
knowledge: Clearcutting removes all trees at once: cheap, but it increases erosion, raises stream temperatures and removes habitat.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: The Green Revolution
objectives: Describe the Green Revolution and its benefits and costs.
knowledge: High-yield crops, synthetic fertilizer, irrigation, pesticides and mechanization raised food production.
Costs include monocultures, loss of genetic diversity, fertilizer runoff and fossil fuel use.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Impacts of Agricultural Practices
objectives: Describe the environmental effects of tilling, slash-and-burn farming and fertilizer use.
knowledge: Tilling breaks up soil and leaves it open to erosion; slash-and-burn clears forest and releases carbon.
Excess fertilizer runs off into water.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Irrigation Methods
objectives: Compare irrigation methods by efficiency and explain salinization, waterlogging and aquifer depletion.
knowledge: About 70% of global freshwater use is agriculture.
Drip irrigation is the most efficient; flood and furrow irrigation lose water to evaporation and runoff; overirrigation causes waterlogging and salinization.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries
topics.clarified2026: EK wording refined (2026-27): about 70% of global freshwater use is agriculture

topics.title: Pest Control Methods
objectives: Describe pesticide use, its effects, and how pests become resistant.
knowledge: Pesticides kill target and nontarget organisms; survivors with resistance breed, so a population becomes resistant.
Genetically modified crops can reduce some pesticide use.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Meat Production Methods
objectives: Compare concentrated animal feeding operations with rotational and free-range grazing, and explain overgrazing and desertification.
knowledge: CAFOs produce meat cheaply but concentrate manure and use antibiotics; free-range and rotational grazing spread the impact.
Overgrazing can lead to desertification; eating less ruminant meat lowers land use and methane.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries
topics.clarified2026: EK wording refined (2026-27): CAFOs vs rotational and free-range grazing, trade-offs, overgrazing, desertification, eating less ruminant meat

topics.title: Impacts of Overfishing
objectives: Explain how overfishing and bycatch deplete fish stocks and food webs.
knowledge: Fishing faster than a stock can reproduce leads to fishery collapse.
Bycatch kills nontarget species, and trawling damages the sea floor.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Impacts of Mining
objectives: Describe surface and subsurface mining and their environmental effects.
knowledge: Surface mining removes overburden to reach ore near the surface; subsurface mining reaches deep deposits at more risk to miners.
Tailings and acid mine drainage pollute water; land reclamation restores mined land.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Impacts of Urbanization
objectives: Describe how urbanization changes land, water and climate.
knowledge: Impervious surfaces raise runoff and flooding and cut infiltration.
Cities can draw down coastal aquifers (saltwater intrusion) and form urban heat islands; urban sprawl spreads development outward.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Ecological Footprints
objectives: Compare ecological and carbon footprints and calculate one from consumption data.
knowledge: An ecological footprint is the land and water area needed to supply what a person uses and absorb the waste.
A carbon footprint counts greenhouse gas emissions only.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Introduction to Sustainability
objectives: Explain sustainability, sustainable yield and environmental indicators.
knowledge: Sustainability means meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs.
Maximum sustainable yield is the largest harvest that leaves a population able to replace it.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Methods to Reduce Urban Runoff
objectives: Describe methods to reduce urban runoff and how each works.
knowledge: Permeable pavement, rain gardens, green roofs and planted areas let water infiltrate instead of running off.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Integrated Pest Management
objectives: Describe integrated pest management and its trade-offs.
knowledge: IPM combines biological, physical and limited chemical controls, monitored over time, to keep pests below harmful levels.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Sustainable Agriculture
objectives: Describe soil conservation practices and how each protects soil.
knowledge: Contour plowing, terracing, windbreaks, strip cropping, no-till farming, crop rotation and perennial crops reduce erosion or restore nutrients.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Aquaculture
objectives: Describe aquaculture and its benefits and drawbacks.
knowledge: Fish farming takes pressure off wild stocks but can concentrate waste, spread disease and let farmed fish escape.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Sustainable Forestry
objectives: Describe sustainable forestry practices.
knowledge: Selective cutting, reforestation, prescribed burns and using recycled wood reduce the harm of logging.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Renewable and Nonrenewable Resources
objectives: Classify energy sources as renewable or nonrenewable.
knowledge: Nonrenewable sources (fossil fuels, nuclear) form far more slowly than they are used; renewable sources (sun, wind, water, biomass) are replenished on human timescales.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Global Energy Consumption
objectives: Describe patterns of global energy consumption by fuel and by country.
knowledge: Fossil fuels supply most of the world's energy; use per person is highest in developed countries.
Use rises as developing countries industrialize.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Fuel Types and Uses
objectives: Describe the fuels people use, from wood to coal, oil and natural gas, and what each is used for.
knowledge: Coal ranks from lignite to bituminous to anthracite by energy content; natural gas is mostly methane and burns cleanest of the fossil fuels.
Cogeneration uses waste heat as well as electricity.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Distribution of Natural Energy Resources
objectives: Explain why energy resources are unevenly spread and what that means for use.
knowledge: Fossil fuel deposits, sunlight, wind and geothermal heat vary by place, which shapes what each country uses.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Fossil Fuels
objectives: Describe how fossil fuels are extracted and burned to make electricity, and the environmental effects, including fracking.
knowledge: A power plant burns fuel to boil water; the steam turns a turbine that spins a generator.
Fracking can contaminate groundwater and release volatile chemicals; tar sands need much energy and water to process.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries
topics.clarified2026: EK wording refined (2026-27): fracking can contaminate groundwater and release VOCs

topics.title: Nuclear Power
objectives: Explain nuclear fission, radioactive decay and half-life, and the benefits and risks of nuclear power.
knowledge: Fission of uranium-235 releases heat to make steam; no carbon dioxide is released in operation.
Radioactive waste stays dangerous for many half-lives; accidents are rare but severe.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Energy from Biomass
objectives: Describe energy from biomass and biofuels and their effects.
knowledge: Burning wood, charcoal, crop waste or dung releases carbon dioxide and particles; ethanol and biodiesel are liquid biofuels.
Biomass is renewable only if it is regrown as fast as it is used.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Solar Energy
objectives: Describe photovoltaic, active and passive solar energy and their trade-offs.
knowledge: Photovoltaic cells turn sunlight directly into electricity; active and passive solar heat buildings and water.
Solar needs storage or backup because sunlight varies.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Hydroelectric Power
objectives: Describe hydroelectric power and its effects on rivers and ecosystems.
knowledge: Water held behind a dam falls through turbines; run-of-the-river and tidal systems use flowing water.
Dams flood land, block fish migration and trap sediment.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Geothermal Energy
objectives: Describe geothermal energy and ground source heat pumps.
knowledge: Heat from Earth's interior can make steam for electricity where it is near the surface.
Ground source heat pumps move heat between a building and the ground.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Hydrogen Fuel Cell
objectives: Describe how a hydrogen fuel cell works and its trade-offs.
knowledge: A fuel cell combines hydrogen and oxygen to make electricity, with water as the product.
Making hydrogen takes energy, often from natural gas; storing it is hard.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Wind Energy
objectives: Describe wind energy and its trade-offs.
knowledge: Wind turns turbine blades that spin a generator; wind farms can share land with farming.
Wind is intermittent and turbines can kill birds and bats.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Energy Conservation
objectives: Describe ways to conserve energy and calculate the savings.
knowledge: Energy-efficient appliances, better insulation, smarter thermostats and lower-energy transport cut energy use.
Savings are calculated from energy, cost and emissions per unit.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Introduction to Air Pollution
objectives: Describe the major air pollutants, their sources, and primary and secondary pollutants.
knowledge: Primary pollutants are emitted directly; secondary pollutants form in the air.
The Clean Air Act sets limits for the criteria pollutants.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Photochemical Smog
objectives: Explain how photochemical smog forms from nitrogen oxides and VOCs in sunlight, through a day.
knowledge: Morning traffic emits NO; it forms NO2, which sunlight splits to make ground-level ozone, peaking in the afternoon.
VOCs keep ozone from being broken down.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Thermal Inversion
objectives: Explain how a thermal inversion traps pollution near the ground.
knowledge: Normally air cools with height; in an inversion a warm layer sits over cool air and stops it rising, trapping pollutants.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Atmospheric CO2 and Particulates
objectives: Describe natural sources of carbon dioxide and particulates.
knowledge: Volcanoes, forest fires, decomposition and dust storms release carbon dioxide and particles without human help.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Indoor Air Pollutants
objectives: Describe indoor air pollutants and their sources.
knowledge: Radon seeps from rock, formaldehyde off-gasses from furniture, carbon monoxide comes from poor combustion, and asbestos fibers come from old buildings.
Indoor pollution is a large health risk where people burn wood or dung to cook.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Reduction of Air Pollutants
objectives: Match methods to reduce air pollutants with the pollutant each removes and how it works.
knowledge: Scrubbers remove sulfur dioxide and particles; catalytic converters turn NOx, CO and hydrocarbons into less harmful gases; electrostatic precipitators and baghouses remove particles.
Vapor recovery nozzles capture gasoline vapor (VOCs) at the pump, not exhaust.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Acid Rain
objectives: Explain how acid deposition forms from NOx and SOx and its effects on soils, lakes and buildings.
knowledge: Nitrogen and sulfur oxides react in the air to form nitric and sulfuric acid that fall as acid deposition.
Limestone bedrock and soils buffer acid; places without it are hit harder.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Noise Pollution
objectives: Describe noise pollution and its effects on wildlife and people.
knowledge: Noise above about 85 decibels harms hearing; noise also disrupts animal communication, migration and predator avoidance.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Sources of Pollution
objectives: Distinguish point and nonpoint sources of pollution.
knowledge: A point source has one identifiable outlet; a nonpoint source is diffuse, like runoff from farms and streets.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Human Impacts on Ecosystems
objectives: Describe how pollution affects aquatic ecosystems, including coral bleaching, oil spills and ocean plastics.
knowledge: Species differ in their tolerance; indicator species signal water quality.
Warming and pollution bleach corals; oil spills smother wildlife; plastics break into microplastics.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Endocrine Disruptors
objectives: Describe how endocrine disruptors interfere with hormones.
knowledge: Endocrine disruptors mimic or block hormones and can harm reproduction and development at low doses.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Human Impacts on Wetlands and Mangroves
objectives: Explain the services wetlands and mangroves provide and how people damage them.
knowledge: Wetlands store floodwater, filter pollutants and are nurseries for fish; mangroves protect coasts from storm surge.
Draining, filling and coastal development destroy them.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Eutrophication
objectives: Explain the full eutrophication chain from nutrient runoff to a dead zone.
knowledge: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus feed an algal bloom; when the algae die, decomposers use up dissolved oxygen, causing hypoxia and fish kills.
An oligotrophic lake is low in nutrients; a eutrophic lake is high.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Thermal Pollution
objectives: Explain thermal pollution and why warm water holds less oxygen.
knowledge: Power plants and factories return heated cooling water; warm water holds less dissolved oxygen and can cause thermal shock.
Thermal pollution is heat, not chemicals.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs)
objectives: Describe persistent organic pollutants and why they last and travel.
knowledge: POPs are fat-soluble, break down slowly and travel long distances in air and water.
DDT and PCBs are examples.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Bioaccumulation and Biomagnification
objectives: Explain bioaccumulation in one organism and biomagnification up a food chain, and calculate concentrations.
knowledge: Bioaccumulation is the buildup of a substance in one organism over its life.
Biomagnification is the rise in concentration at each higher trophic level, so top predators carry the most.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Solid Waste Disposal
objectives: Describe how solid waste is disposed of in landfills and incinerators, and their effects.
knowledge: A sanitary landfill has a liner, a leachate collection system and a cover; landfill gas is mostly methane.
Incineration reduces volume but releases air pollutants and ash.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Waste Reduction Methods
objectives: Describe ways to reduce waste and their trade-offs.
knowledge: Source reduction, reuse, recycling and composting keep waste out of landfills.
Landfill gas can be captured to generate electricity.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Sewage Treatment
objectives: Describe the stages of sewage treatment and what each removes.
knowledge: Primary treatment settles solids; secondary treatment uses bacteria to break down organic matter; tertiary treatment removes nutrients and other pollutants.
Disinfection kills pathogens before release.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Lethal Dose 50% (LD50)
objectives: Explain and read LD50, the dose that kills half a test population.
knowledge: LD50 is the dose, usually in mg per kg of body mass, that kills 50% of a test population; a lower LD50 means a more toxic substance.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Dose Response Curve
objectives: Read a dose-response curve, including the threshold dose and LD50.
knowledge: A dose-response curve plots the percent of a test population responding against dose.
The threshold dose is the highest dose with no observed effect.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Pollution and Human Health
objectives: Explain why the health effects of pollution are hard to measure, and how pollutants combine.
knowledge: People are exposed to many substances at once, so a single cause is hard to prove.
Synergism is when two substances together do more harm than the sum of each; acute effects come fast, chronic effects after long exposure.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Pathogens and Infectious Diseases
objectives: Describe pathogens, how infectious diseases spread, and how environmental change affects them.
knowledge: Pathogens are organisms that cause disease; vectors such as mosquitoes carry some of them.
Warming can spread vectors into new areas; poor sanitation spreads waterborne disease.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Stratospheric Ozone Depletion
objectives: Explain how chlorofluorocarbons destroy stratospheric ozone and the effects of more UV radiation.
knowledge: UV light frees chlorine from CFCs; one chlorine atom destroys many ozone molecules in a cycle.
Less ozone lets more UV reach the surface, raising skin cancer and cataract risk.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Reducing Ozone Depletion
objectives: Describe how the Montreal Protocol and CFC replacements reduced ozone depletion.
knowledge: The Montreal Protocol phased out CFCs; replacement HCFCs and HFCs deplete less or no ozone, though HFCs are strong greenhouse gases.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: The Greenhouse Effect
objectives: Explain the greenhouse effect: greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit infrared radiation from Earth's surface.
knowledge: Sunlight warms the surface, which gives off infrared radiation; greenhouse gases absorb it and warm the lower atmosphere.
Global warming potential compares gases with carbon dioxide; the greenhouse effect is not the ozone layer.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Increases in the Greenhouse Gases
objectives: Describe the human sources of greenhouse gases and the evidence that their levels are rising.
knowledge: Burning fossil fuels, deforestation, agriculture and landfills add carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide.
Ice cores and direct measurements show carbon dioxide rising steeply since industrialization.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Global Climate Change
objectives: Explain the effects of climate change and the feedback loops that amplify it.
knowledge: Effects include higher temperatures, melting land ice, sea level rise, shifting ranges and extreme weather.
Melting sea ice lowers albedo and thawing permafrost releases methane: positive feedback loops.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Ocean Warming
objectives: Explain the causes and effects of ocean warming.
knowledge: The ocean absorbs most of the extra heat; warmer water expands and holds less oxygen.
Warming bleaches corals and shifts species ranges and ocean circulation.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Ocean Acidification
objectives: Explain how rising carbon dioxide lowers ocean pH and harms organisms that build carbonate shells.
knowledge: Carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater to form carbonic acid, releasing hydrogen ions and lowering pH.
Fewer carbonate ions make it harder for corals and shellfish to build calcium carbonate.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Invasive Species
objectives: Explain why invasive species thrive and how they harm ecosystems.
knowledge: Invasive species are often generalists and r-selected, and spread where they meet no natural predators or diseases.
They outcompete native species; control is hard and costly.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Endangered Species
objectives: Describe what makes species endangered and how laws and treaties protect them.
knowledge: Specialists, species with low reproduction and those that need large ranges are most at risk.
The Endangered Species Act and CITES protect species and their trade.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

topics.title: Human Impacts on Biodiversity
objectives: Explain the main human threats to biodiversity and ways to reduce them.
knowledge: HIPPCO names the threats: habitat loss, invasive species, pollution, human population growth, climate change and overexploitation.
Wildlife corridors and protected areas reconnect habitat fragments.
topics.source: Course at a Glance poster (official title); objectives and knowledge are our summaries

skillsTopics.title: Scientific Notation and Metric Prefixes
objectives: Write large and small numbers in scientific notation, read scale words such as million and billion, and use metric prefixes.
knowledge: 2.5 million is 2.5 × 10^6; multiply by adding exponents and divide by subtracting them.
Kilo- means 10^3, mega- 10^6, giga- 10^9; milli- means 10^-3.

skillsTopics.title: Rates and Per-Capita Values
objectives: Compute rates per unit time, per unit area and per person, and move between totals and per-capita values.
knowledge: A rate divides an amount by time (or area, or people): kcal per square meter per year.
Per capita means per person: total divided by population.

skillsTopics.title: Unit Conversions and Dimensional Analysis
objectives: Convert units with conversion factors written as fractions so the units cancel, including energy units.
knowledge: Write each conversion factor as a fraction equal to 1, arranged so the unwanted unit cancels.
Common energy units: joule, kilocalorie, kilowatt-hour, BTU.

skillsTopics.title: Percents and Percent Change
objectives: Find a percent of a quantity and compute percent change with the difference in parentheses, divided by the original value, times 100.
knowledge: Percent change = (new - old) / old × 100: the subtraction happens before the division.
A percent of a quantity is the percent as a decimal times the quantity.

skillsTopics.title: Growth Rates, Doubling Time and the Rule of 70
objectives: Use the rule of 70 to find a doubling time and add it to a start year; relate a growth rate in percent to doubling.
knowledge: Doubling time is about 70 divided by the growth rate in percent per year.
If a question asks "in what year", add the doubling time to the start year.
